title: Desktop UI automation
summary: The optional ui skill inspects and operates native accessibility controls on the selected Gateway. Enable Desktop UI in capability controls, then discover ui. Existing saved capability.
html:
Desktop UI automation

The optional ui skill inspects and operates native accessibility controls on the selected Gateway. Enable Desktop UI in capability controls, then discover ui. Existing saved capability selections are preserved. ui.status reports availability independently of enablement; headless Gateways remain usable for other skills.

Use accessibility semantics first: find a button and invoke it, set an ordinary field value, select a row, or set a checkbox to a desired state. The normal Agent reasons about the request; matching, traversal, waiting and input dispatch are deterministic. No helper model or agent runs.

Ownership and discovery

Owner Responsibility
desktop Application/process lifecycle and top-level window geometry/focus
screen Display geometry, screenshots, OCR and screen context
clipboard Explicit clipboard reads and writes
browser Managed or explicitly attached browser page DOM; prefer this for page controls
ui Native accessibility elements and explicit bounded keyboard/pointer fallback

Entry tools are ui.status, ui.snapshot, ui.find, and ui.focused_element. Four sections expose the rest of the surface:

Section Operations (prefix each with ui.)
ui.inspect status, snapshot, find, element, focused_element
ui.semantic_actions focus, invoke, set_value, select, toggle, expand_collapse, scroll
ui.input key_press, type_text, pointer_move, pointer_click, pointer_scroll, drag, draw_path
ui.wait wait_for

All tools use the existing skill contract, capability policy, permission policy, execution receipts and cancellation. Read operations include waits; every other operation is an external write with ordinary confirmation metadata. A control can submit, delete or charge money; its name is not proof of safety. No additional approval dialog or model classifier exists.

Native prerequisites and limitations

Platform Semantic adapter Input Prerequisites and verification
Windows UI Automation through comtypes and native UIA patterns Win32 input, physical pixels Interactive logged-in user; session 0 unavailable. UIPI and UAC/Secure Desktop remain authoritative. Implemented; native validation pending. Windows hardware tests are not a release requirement.
macOS Accessibility attributes/actions through PyObjC Permission-gated Quartz output, native points System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility for the Gateway host. Probes never prompt. Semantic operations need neither Screen Recording nor Input Monitoring. Real macOS smoke must run on macOS before release validation.
Linux X11 AT-SPI through PyGObject XTEST output plus semantic text insertion Graphical session, session accessibility bus, AT-SPI typelib and Python gi; XTEST is probed separately. Distribution packages commonly include python3-gi, gir1.2-atspi-2.0, and at-spi2-core. The Gateway interpreter must be able to import them.
Linux Wayland AT-SPI where available No keyboard/pointer fallback No XWayland or compositor-policy bypass. AT-SPI windows can have UI-owned signed IDs where Desktop lacks native window support.

Linux X11 and macOS acceptance determine Desktop Vision release readiness. Mac validation requires the real selected Gateway, an awake interactive desktop and existing capture/input permissions. Native support also depends on the target application's accessible interfaces; unsupported actions return ui.action_unsupported.

Guarded visual input

Use visual_target from vision.locate instead of a raw screenshot-derived point. Pointer move, click, scroll, shortcuts and typing accept this target; drag accepts visual start/end targets. The Gateway derives coordinates from its own capture record, serializes input, rechecks native permissions, layout and surface ownership, then recaptures the same scope. The selected rectangle plus a 16-source-pixel margin must match exactly. Unrelated pixels can change. A changed target returns ui_visual_target_stale before dispatch; recapture and locate again. Animated controls and blinking carets can therefore require a stable target region or a semantic action.

On macOS, the final ownership check uses AppKit's native mouse hit test; Quartz rectangles alone include noninteractive Dock surfaces. It uses capture-owned window IDs without associating them with AX elements by title or approximate bounds. Linux includes unmanaged X11 overlays in its surface stack and prevents input when ownership cannot be established. Visual input defaults to a 30-second validation/input deadline; an explicit timeout_ms overrides it. Legacy calls retain their 10-second default.

Typing and shortcuts also verify focus, including during bounded input chunks. Linux text is preflighted against the active keymap before any character is sent. ui_text_unrepresentable permits an explicit Clipboard write followed by a fresh guarded paste shortcut when authorized. Report the clipboard change; never restore over a later user change. Known secure controls retain credential handoff. Appearance alone cannot establish that a remote field is non-secure.

After dispatch, older targets are invalidated. Loss of a response remains an uncertain effect; never replay automatically. A successful dispatch is not task success: verify semantic state or capture fresh pixels and use vision.compare. OS capture and input remain separate operations.

The Gateway advertises ui_status even when native access is unavailable. Other tags are ui_accessibility, ui_keyboard, ui_pointer, and ui_drag; they are reported only after current prerequisites are checked. Configured tags cannot invent support. Saved run capability snapshots retain existing semantics, and the Gateway rechecks current session/permission support on every operation, including calls after resume.

ui_draw_path is advertised by Gateways with both native drag support and the Screen service. It is separate from ui_drag so older Gateways do not advertise continuous path support. Guarded drawing also requires enabled Screen capture and screen_observation_v2 / ui_visual_targets, under the existing visual-input authorization checks.

Linux dependencies remain optional so a headless installation does not require GTK/GI build libraries. The ui-linux Python extra installs PyGObject when the native GI development prerequisites are present; distribution-provided GI packages must match the Gateway interpreter. GTK3 is required only for the included purpose-built smoke fixture, not for the UI service.

Elements, locators and references

snapshot defaults to the active window. An exact scope.window_id from Desktop selects that window without focusing it. scope.application_id restricts the selected window and scope.ancestor_ref restricts descendants to an observed element. It does not launch an app.

Elements contain a normalized role/control type, name, label, automation ID, bounded value summary, states, bounds, supported actions and opaque ref. They include ui_revision, window_id, and application_id. Native object handles are private.

Locators use literal role, name, label, automation_id, control_type, ordinary value, and state predicates. Matching is exact by default; exact=false means case-insensitive substring matching. No regex, platform query language, code, or model ranking is accepted. For example:

{"scope":{"window_id":"<desktop window ID>"},"locator":{"role":"textbox","label":"Project Name"}}

find returns all matches within its bound; a mutation requires exactly one match. An incomplete traversal cannot prove a locator unique and therefore cannot authorize that mutation. An exact reference can identify an already observed control in a larger tree.

References are random server-side IDs scoped to the Gateway service instance, desktop/window and native element lifetime, conversation, run, and structural tree revision. They expire after 60 seconds. Changing structure, replacing a native object, closing/recreating a window, changing Gateway/owner, or restarting the Gateway invalidates the ref. Every use reobserves the bounded tree and compares the retained native identity. Ordinary value/state changes preserve identity. ui.element_stale requires a new snapshot/find and deliberate choice of a new reference. The service never substitutes a similar label or first match.

Actions and input

Use ui.invoke for a primary semantic action. set_value replaces ordinary editable text. toggle and select accept boolean desired; expand_collapse accepts expanded or collapsed. Already satisfied desired states do not send another native action. scroll uses native scroll/value interfaces, with a bounded direction and amount.

Keyboard input requires an exact already-focused non-secure target; use ui.focus explicitly first. key_press accepts one key with up to four distinct modifiers (CTRL, ALT, SHIFT, META). Keys include letters, digits, navigation keys, SPACE, and F1–F12. macOS letter/digit chords currently use ANSI virtual-key positions. type_text inserts ordinary text without reading or overwriting the clipboard.

Pointer tools are explicit fallback. pointer_click accepts either a current element ref (clickable center calculated from current bounds) or a point. Points must declare:

Space Meaning
screen_physical Global physical desktop pixels on Windows/X11; negative monitor origins are valid
screen_logical Display-local logical offsets plus a Screen display_id; translated with that display's scale and origin
window_client Client-local pixels plus exact Desktop window_id, on Windows/X11

macOS accepts logical points with a display ID; ambiguous global physical pixels on mixed-scale displays and client coordinates without a proven client mapping are rejected. Returned AX bounds are global native points. UI reuses Screen's display metadata without capturing pixels. Drag duration is 100–5000 ms and 2–100 steps. Cancellation always attempts to release held buttons and modifiers; native OS focus and permission policies still apply.

Drawing on a canvas

ui.draw_path draws one continuous left-button stroke on a focused canvas. Pass its current visual_target from vision.locate, an ordered points_image array of 2–256 {x, y} points, and optionally duration_ms (100–5000; default 1000). Points are in the original capture's image pixels and must all lie inside the target's bbox_image. The Gateway owns the image-to-native mapping. It checks fresh canvas pixels, every vertex and every segment's surface ownership before sending input. A narrow overlay between vertices also rejects the stroke. Native hit tests are applied to vertices on platforms that require them. These checks precede dispatch; observation and input are not atomic, and a window can still change during a stroke.

The pointer follows the supplied polyline with equal time between vertices; sample curves with enough points for the intended smoothness. Repeat the first point at the end to close a shape. Keep a margin for brush width. The tool does not select brushes, generate artwork or save files.

For a drawing task, launch/focus the requested application with Desktop, select its drawing tool through semantic UI or fresh visual targets, capture with geometry_version=2, and locate the drawable canvas. Plan the requested geometry within that canvas. Prefer the app's shape tools when useful; use draw_path for arbitrary strokes. Capture and locate again between strokes, then use vision.compare to assess the result. A successful tool receipt confirms input dispatch, not visual correctness. Cancellation or failure releases the button but can leave a partial stroke; observe before deciding whether an explicit undo or another action is appropriate.

Secure fields and external text

Secure fields return the fixed <secure> marker. Native secure status is checked before requesting any backing value; secret-value locators never match. Ordinary set_value, type_text, and key_press reject secure fields. No set_secret tool is exposed because this transport has no private post-model Parameter Store binding. Use the existing ask_user checkpoint to have the user enter credentials directly in the application, then confirm completion. Never ask for passwords in chat.

For guarded macOS typing, the expected application's focused accessibility control and its parents are checked directly, without reading values or scanning unrelated applications. Quartz does not expose a key-window flag: when the foreground application has a visible floating or modal panel below the Dock layer, visual keyboard input fails closed rather than assuming its ordinary document still owns focus. Use a verified semantic element in the panel, or dismiss the panel and obtain a fresh observation.

Names, values, labels and dialog text are untrusted external data. Tool results retain their data role and content_trust=untrusted_external_data; app text cannot become runtime policy or system/developer instructions. Exact ordinary arguments and observations remain in normal execution/result evidence, but activity diagnostics, model debug traces and portable handoff omit UI payloads even when optional redaction is disabled. Secure backing values never enter that evidence. UI content is not automatically copied into Memory or Working Context.

There is no keyboard capture, event recorder, continuous accessibility stream, screenshot, background screen surveillance, clipboard paste implementation, shell script, or native-code injection surface in this skill.

Bounds, cancellation and unknown outcomes

Snapshot output is capped at 500 elements and depth 32; defaults are 200 elements and depth 8. Names/labels/value summaries are capped at 512 characters; ordinary input text at 4096. The native scan is capped at 2000 nodes/depth 32; wire results at 2 MiB. Resource budgets are clamped, unknown fields are rejected, and omitted nodes report truncated=true with returned_nodes and the observed match_count where applicable.

Timeouts are 1–60000 ms. wait_for polls inside one Gateway call, at 50–1000 ms intervals, for appearance/disappearance or boolean states. A stale ref always fails; use a locator to wait for disappearance. No Agent turns or helper inference are used by polling.

One native operation owns the input gate at a time. A deadline bounds the caller even if a provider is blocked. The gate stays occupied until that provider actually returns, preventing overlapping input after a timeout. Cancellation checks occur between native calls; an individual OS call cannot always be interrupted. There is no forced termination of the target application.

After input dispatch begins, a cancellation, native failure, or lost response returns an uncertain outcome (executed=null, effect_unknown=true, remote_effect_possible=true). Never replay invoke, type, key, click or drag automatically. Inspect snapshot/element explicitly and reconcile. Desired-state actions may be retried only after fresh observations. Normal runtime journals block repeated unresolved mutations; the Gateway also rejects reused execution IDs within its bounded recent-ID cache. This cache is not durable replay authority.

Transport, errors and source ownership

Authenticated POST /ui/operation carries a closed operation/arguments envelope plus runtime node, conversation, run and execution identities. POST /ui/cancel targets the same Gateway. Inbound and outbound forwarding share schemas, sanitized errors, exact node checks and one-shot dispatch. No controller-local fallback exists.

Canonical Error Catalog aliases cover ui.accessibility_unavailable, permission/session/adapter failures, missing/ambiguous/stale/hidden/disabled elements, unsupported actions, forbidden secure reads or secret binding, keyboard/pointer/coordinate errors, timeout/cancel, missing target capability, uncertain outcome, invalid requests/responses, transport loss, busy and duplicate IDs. Each has catalog remediation; native exception text is never returned.

skills/ui owns catalog declarations and selected-Gateway dispatch. gateway_core/ui/contract.py owns schemas; service.py owns refs, waits and execution state; adapter.py owns normalized traversal/geometry; linux.py, macos.py, and windows.py own native APIs. Shared Gateway, authorization, cancellation, Error Catalog and content policy remain authoritative.
